An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting a structural variation that aligns with the Galactic plane's orientation. A basic model of the related minimization equation supports the hypothesis that this anisotropy results from both bipolar components - one related to the Galactic disk and another to the magnetic equator. Furthermore, combining the related anisotropy parameters with cosmic ray anisotropy studies and the related spectral characteristics offers valuable insights for both existing and upcoming theoretical models of the most energetic cosmic rays.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific measure, $\Psi_2^p$, related to the angle and magnitude of the direction in which particles move, relative to a specific line, determined by rigid-body motion, in collisions between lead ions at various energies up to 2.76 TeV per nucleon pair. Analyzing the collision of two discs of matter can reveal that the angle and magnitude of movement fluctuate, and if a quark-gluon plasma is created, these fluctuations may provide valuable insights into its internal properties. The researchers found significant correlations between different powers of $1/\tan(\Delta \phi/2)$ were predicted by the "two-component" model but a new approach, the "hydrodynamic" one, underpinned by viscous hydrodynamics fails to explain the observed correlations, and the energy loss of fast-moving particles carries a similar message.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables, particularly those containing missing values and structural issues like functional dependencies and key constraints. Unlike conventional methods that assume pre-existing data quality, our approach allows for the resolution of inconsistencies in tables with varying levels of data completeness, while taking into consideration table-level data qualities. To achieve this, we incorporate data qualities into theories like Armstrong's axioms and explore their impact on reasoning, including closure computation and query answering. Answering these questions requires developing new algorithms for both simple and conjunctive queries, accounting for inconsistencies in data tables. To validate our solutions, we implemented a prototype in Python and evaluated its performance through empirical experiments.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose where a grasped object's reference frame aligns with the
demonstration's reference frame. In order to validate our approach, we develop a
simulation-based experiment that compares our method to end-to-end learning
policies without any object-specific generalization capabilities. Furthermore,
we present a substantial dataset comprising 3D demonstrations and static 7-DoF
datasets, both covering the Neural Descriptor Field (NDF) format. This data was
generated using a narrow-body manipulator in a real-world setting and is publicly
available online at http://www.neuraldescriptorfields.de.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined, regardless of individual transit signals, which become negligible at the level of photometric noise. In order to accurately measure the atmosphere's influence, we examined the residual transits after a recent meteoroid impact and analyzed the resulting data from multiple sources. Initially, we thought the precision achieved (~0.015) was close to its limit, but we discovered that it could be significantly surpassed with an optimal analysis of multiple sources in a wide-field dataset. In order to accurately interpret the results, we developed a comprehensive model that takes into account various factors causing altitude variations in the atmosphere including aerosols, clouds, and air currents, which can either transport or deplete aerosols. This in-depth model is necessary to achieve a precise analysis of wide-field datasets and to better understand the relationships between the different aerosol components.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence constraints utilizing these intermediate cues. This study concentrates on refining two-stage pipelines by combining two distinct concepts: projection grouping on one hand and correspondence learning on the other. We initially employ a patch-based method to forecast projection heatmaps, representing the likelihood distribution of projected corners from 3D bounding boxes. Next, a projection grouping module is proposed to eliminate redundant maxima from these heatmaps. Subsequently, 3D box parameters are adjusted to best align with the reduced maxima through the enforcement of correspondence constraints. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed pipeline, achieving the current record for the ADE200 dataset and ranking third for the NYUv2 dataset.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed precision matrix from multivariate normal
data, with applications in knowledge integration and data compression. Our
GGLasso package extends the original library by supporting general graph forms,
incorporating constraints, and handling various statistical challenges such as
mean and covariance estimation. The package features over twenty preconfigured
optimization configurations and is user-friendly with both basic and advanced
implementation guides for customizing settings. With its versatile capabilities,
GGLasso can be applied to solve a wide range of statistical problems. The package
source code is available at https://github.com/vshaklovitz/GeneralGraphicalLasso.

Numerous numerical methods for solving linear response theories in overdamped stochastic differential equations have been utilized to calculate various stochastic quantities in the study of complex systems, including biomolecules such as DNA and proteins. To accurately assess configurational averaging's impact on biomolecular properties like mobility and friction, new numerical methods were developed that ensure precise computation of configuration-dependent coefficients. Notably, this approach provides accurate estimation of the center of mobility in biomolecules in crowded environments, even in the presence of spatial inhomogeneities caused by macromolecular structure and solvent effects. As an illustration, this method overcame previous inaccuracies in simulating a biomolecule's migratory behavior in a crowded environment when applying linear response theories to simulated trajectories.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes ("pinch-off time") generally hold for both slow-moving and fast-moving spheres, yet require further refinement, especially in the middle speed range. In fact, at mid-range speeds, pinch-off times relate differently to fluid dynamics than they do at either low or high speeds, indicating that increased pressures inside the formed cavity play a significant role. In addition, our findings include the shift from the deeper water-entrapment phenomenon to the surface-seal regime, and observations on the partial-seal, rippling-cavity-surface, and secondary pinch-off stages of water-entry interactions.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and applications in metrology and communication systems. Quantum acoustic resonators serve as the ideal testing ground for multi-phonon phenomena through a combination of theoretical and experimental studies. The specific system studied consists of a semiconductor quantum dot driven by a laser, coupled to an acoustic cavity, and has exhibited remarkable multi-phonon properties, albeit previously described with a simplistic two-level model. However, by accounting for both bright and dark excitons within a comprehensive eight-level model, a more accurate representation emerges. This updated analysis reveals that dark excitons offer a significant advantage over their bright counterparts, with a lower threshold for entering a regime characterized by a backflow of photons, where the quantum dot absorbs energy from the cavity, and where dark excitons play a pivotal role. Furthermore, an even more complex scenario unfolds when considering inescapable exciton decay, where the system exhibits a surprising hysteresis behavior and a reversal of energy flow under certain conditions.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model contains horizontal and vertical hopping terms and reveals two distinct non-equivalent Dirac cones within the first Brillouin zone along a high-symmetry path. These cones can be modified through various perturbations of the Hamiltonian. These perturbations preserve the lattice's symmetry but perturb the non-symmorphic symmetry's preservation, and we found that the Dirac cones collapse into closed non-symmorphic Berry-flux loops. These closed loops can be parametrized and filled by filling factor, and we found that half-filling can flatten the low-energy bands. This process can be visualized using non-symmorphic Bi-chiral graphene strips that, when fully filled, form a 3D metallic structure.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference in specific regions of space. This new method incorporates a space-based target property into the inference framework by incorporating specialized embedding layers for describing 3D chemical structures. A set of embedding methods for spatial chemical structures were evaluated to identify the most effective way to incorporate spatial information into the design of polymers. By utilizing a spatial information pathway in a graph neural network-based regression model, the most suitable chemical descriptor was determined to be a key component for the new design framework. Consequently, a streamlined version of the framework was developed for polymer design based on spatial information, and its efficacy has been demonstrated through a series of benchmark tests involving various chemical structure descriptions and target property predictions, including the accurate design of polymer monomers and post-synthesis modification of small molecules to achieve position-specific properties.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach that solely utilizes CT scans for automatically identifying and outlining tumors in the esophagus with satisfactory precision. To achieve this, we designed an automatic, start-to-finish method based on deep neural networks called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet. This model leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms in dense blocks to pinpoint the most relevant features for classification and outline prediction. It employs dilated convolution operations to manage memory usage while detecting long-range dependencies in very high-resolution images. We tested this model on two datasets consisting of CT scans from patients who underwent surgery for esophageal tumors and found that it could produce highly precise results with dHFD and dHD metrics of 7mm and 14mm, respectively. These results show that a simplified, effective clinical approach starting and ending with CT scans is feasible.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments in processing content that mixes different languages, highlighting limitations and potential improvements, with a focus on vital tasks and challenges, essential resources, and cutting-edge tools and platforms, aiming to identify areas for future improvements in the NLP community.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations from first principles. Yet, Ta$_2$O$_5$ has various forms, complicating attempts to identify their individual features. To resolve this issue, researchers used time-dependent density functional methods to study the energy loss function in Ta$_2$O$_5$, specifically in its optical state, and across different polymorphs. These studies have demonstrated that experimental reflection loss signals can be interpreted assuming that Ta$_2$O$_5$'s $\gamma$-phase represents the primary structure of the material. Notably, researchers have also discovered a previously unrecorded feature in their loss function predictions which they have attributed to an underlying feature of the $\gamma$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structure. This Ta$_2$O$_5$ form includes a metallic component in its composition, a 1 electron deep defect and a surrounding polaron, all present within each Ta atom. This feature was predicted to last indefinitely due to the lack of surface voids in the material's configuration, and ta research has since confirmed its existence.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We conducted a comprehensive analysis, examining over 11 million Twitter users' interactions with a large-scale, politically motivated fake news campaign during a critical period in the 2020 US presidential primary season. By leveraging detailed data and statewide variation in Republican vote share, we were able to estimate the impact of political polarization on misinformation dissemination in different states. Our analysis of this extensive dataset revealed thatConscientiousness, a key component of a person's tendency to engage in civic behavior, played a pivotal role in an individual's willingness to propagate misinformation, but this effect varied significantly across different states and was strongly linked to that state's support for the 2020 Obama re-election campaign. To better understand these complex dynamics, we developed a new metric, the "misinformation-geography index," and used it to analyze the spatial variation in a person's likelihood to spread misinformation. Our findings have broad implications, informing public health campaigns, informing policy-making, and influencing the design of more effective algorithms.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study systematically analyzes audio input from humans teaching robots by examining three key features: speech length, speech content, and non-verbal sounds. Focusing on teaching three distinct skills, the resulting data reveals distinct patterns in audio output, indicating that humans produce sound regardless of whether they feel watched. Furthermore, specific types of sound, particularly non-verbal sounds, are associated with specific skills, potentially signaling to the robot that it should connect those sounds with particular aspects of the task. Consequently, enhancing current silent demonstration techniques with a speaker model could provide the robotic learner with a more comprehensive and flexible set of information to work with.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models. A promising approach to addressing this difficulty is through the use of holographic duality in settings where analytical calculations are feasible. Concentrating on conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, we have employed two viable definitions of complexity - both for quantum states and for operators - to carry out explicit, state-of-the-art feasible calculations of complexity growth.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the vulnerability of hyperlinks and lack of additional information in selected domains, while multi-target CDR could overcome these limitations. Yet, existing multi-target CDR models are constrained to known domains and fail to consider data sparsity across various domains. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel model called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR). This innovative framework partitions domains into well-populated and data-sparse categories and focuses on enhancing ratings in sparse domains through two innovative mechanisms. The first, called cross-domain information aggregation (CDIA), integrates influential multi-target signals without超链接 or详细信息. Subsequently, the second mechanism, sparse-domain influence learning (SDIL), is designed to enhance the representation of Recommender systems (RS) by integrating domain-specific and general information. We evaluate our proposed model across four diverse data sets, and the experimental findings demonstrate that MSDCR consistently surpasses eight state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in both single-domain and cross-domain recommendation tasks.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable quality control pipelines, but effectively generalizing these methods across diverse, previously unseen data remains a significant challenge. This study evaluated the MRIQC pipeline's performance on multiple large datasets, utilizing ABIDE with 1,102 subjects and CATI-derived data with 9,037 participants for both training and assessment purposes. Our investigation focused on describing the characteristics of high and low quality data identified by MRIQC, both manually and automatically, both within the training and unseen populations. Furthermore, we examined the extent to which implicit data metadata influences the pipeline's data classification. Our results are meant to guide future MRI data generalizability research.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate our approach's effectiveness and we explored the underlying mechanisms of vehicle-to-grid interaction using a case study.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes as we move from Gd to Cm due to differences in 5d and 4f electron localization. Based on the full-potential calculated formation energies, we predict that all GdxCm1-xSn3 materials are thermodynamically viable and maintain the same AuCu3 crystal structure. We created phase diagrams to study the relative stability of these compounds against elemental decomposition and alternative crystal structures, finding that they are most stable in the AuCu3 form. Furthermore, the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave + U method outperforms the local density approximation in describing the magnetic behavior and accurately positioning the magnetism in these materials.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical phenomena are predicted to occur, including bileptons and three types of heavy quarks: ${\cal D}$, ${\cal S}$, and ${\cal T}$. Theoretical calculations suggest that Quantum Chromodynamics will result in heavy quarks bonding to each other or light quarks to form composite particles like baryons and mesons that might be detectable with a next-generation 100 TeV particle accelerator or even a high-intensity proton beam directional collider.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between the standard ordered generating sequences, Coxeter length, and the descent set of Bn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within haloes $\rho(r)$. Based on these findings and an N-body simulation, we calculated the lensing influence on supernova magnitudes and confirmed their agreement. Additionally, we calculated the lensing-induced shear and convergence correlation with the residual Hubble diagram types Ia supernova.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit ~1 GHz levels of spectral diffusion without the need for extensive optimization of the fabrication process.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The impact of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
An new isolated input model is proposed that can be compared to the model with
the complete feature map as the baseline.
It is found that the proposed model is slightly inferior, indicating that the
context has both a positive and negative effect on the performance.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon v_i$ in a bounded, smooth domain in $\mathbb{R}^4$, with a given distance function, bounded domain, smooth functions, and conditions on $x$ and $\beta$. Here, $u$ and $v$ are sets of functions in a Sobolev space, and $m$ is a positive function. By using a mountain pass theorem and perturbation theory, we can establish the existence of a system of solutions under specific conditions on $f$ and $\varepsilon$. Additionally, by using a change of variable, we can establish the existence of a positive distance function that is less than one. Here, $u$ and $v$ are sets of functions in a Sobolev space, and $m$ is a positive function.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties, but these methods come with potential complications and higher mortality rates. At the 66th Annual Meeting of the Society for Mathematics Chemistry and Physics, a cohort-based stochastic model is presented, aligning with data from the United States Organ Sharing system, focusing on desensitization kidney transplants from non-matching donors. A key aspect of this model is the incorporation of a desensitization approach that matches the characteristics of the RADICAL trial, an industry-standard reference. This model is used to analyze the impact of various trial parameters on transplant success, offering insights into potential improvements for this research. Additionally, it can aid in planning future kidney transplants by considering desensitization.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical analysis of the word2vec model, a prominent NLP technique for representing semantic relationships between words. A meticulous examination of the model's learning process is undertaken, involving the derivation of its objective function from its underlying components. A resulting expression for the objective function is obtained, offering insights into the underlying assumptions of the model. Notably, the model's performance is found to be heavily influenced by the structure of the corpus being analyzed, with specific mathematical implications being explored. Furthermore, previous research on the model is reviewed and summarized, primarily focusing on empirically based studies.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior, a less explored area, is another significant goal. This paper investigates these goals within a general framework of partial observability, stochasticity, and potentially selfish agents. Specifically, it delves into the feasibility of simultaneously teaching all involved agents both rationalizable outcomes and correlated equilibria in partially observable Markov games. Under certain assumptions about the environment's structure, it is demonstrated that the set rCE encompasses a broader range of behaviors than the CE set, while also providing a stochastic structure to achieve CE that scales polynomially with the state and action spaces' sizes.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are multiple possible outcomes for the infected population at the point of collapse, a result that displays the oscillatory behaviour commonly seen in stochastic systems.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning the format of experimental data is a straightforward process, reconciling disparate theoretical predictions is a more complex task. Given the numerous contributors to different physical processes, such as parton distribution functions, evolution effects, and higher-order corrections, it is essential to combine these predictions in an efficient manner. Given their varied outputs, such as cross-sections, asymmetries, and momenta transfers, and associated uncertainties, scripts must be capable of producing unified inputs with combined uncertainty ranges. Given the numerous datasets and processes being fitted, these automated integration tools must be scalable to large fitting procedures. This research develops general, automated integration tools that are capable of efficiently combining PDF effects with other parameters in both Monte Carlo and mean-variance formats, and can be used to fit PDFs to both public and private datasets, such as those from the LHC and the Tevatron, and is demonstrated by fitting data from the W and Z boson production processes.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current approach equally values all collected observations, neglecting their varying significance. A more adaptive method, the variance reduction based experience replay framework, selectively leverages the most informative historical data. This approach prioritizes past observations more likely to represent the current target distribution. Theoretical and practical evaluations demonstrate that this method accelerates optimal policy discovery and boosts the effectiveness of state-of-the-art policy optimization methods.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk Dataset. This large 
dataset comprises over 300,000 written conversational dialogue sentences, 
maintaining a high degree of complexity (a 10-way branching factor) along with 
6-way phone call branching points. To facilitate our modeling of dialogue, we 
developed a graph-based representation of conversation that incorporates 
necessary information from telephone calls. Furthermore, our research explores 
various aspects of written and phone call dialogue, including their distinct 
characteristics, the impact of context on dialogue complexity, the influence 
of context on branching possibilities, and the modeling of written dialogue 
subgraphs. All of our models were evaluated using an automatic scoring system 
based on embedding similarity.

We introduce MG-GLAM, a computational tool developed to rapidly create comprehensive N-body simulations for various cosmological theories, specifically modified gravity models. This program builds upon the existing GLAM code and incorporates an advanced multigrid method to solve the non-linear equations characteristic of modified gravity theories, resulting in highly efficient simulations. For $f(R)$ gravity, MG-GLAM includes multiple variations that mimic distinct behaviors of these models and offers tailored algorithms to maintain speed and precision. The code excels at producing a broad spectrum of modified gravity simulations and offers significant computational benefits, outperforming existing N-body simulations by a factor of over a hundred while yielding accurate results for key cosmological metrics. MG-GLAM is suited for creating large sets of modified gravity simulations that can be utilized in Monte Carlo analyses. The code and its various features are thoroughly described, with numerous test cases and a large set of production simulations served as examples.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolving in time on these domains. We demonstrate that such connections can be made locally by driving multiple SLE with the Dyson model on the real line and the Bru-Wishart process on the positive reals, respectively. Ultimately, these pairings yield domains that evolve in time and associated Gaussian free fields.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that converts a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing high-quality manuscripts
and software projects. Originally developed at McMaster University's theoretical
biology lab, WorkingWiki enables multiple users to work together on a range of
tasks by utilizing command-line tools to translate raw'source code' into desired outputs.
Its features cater specifically to programmers and researchers who use languages
like R, Python, and C, and it boasts specialized tools for seamless LaTeX editing.
By integrating features from collaborative editors, development environments,
version control systems, and publishing platforms, WorkingWiki unlocks the
full potential of wiki-based collaboration, and its customizable'makefiles'
and modular architecture enable users to tailor and repurpose its functionality.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of a methane-air jet flame experiencing turbulence to determine its response to acoustic vibrations emitted from upstream, while factoring in temperature fluctuations that can cause instability in flames. To accurately predict flame behavior in a linearized model, it is crucial to account for heat released from the temperature fluctuations. Unlike previous studies using an step-like fuel jet model that ignore this effect, the current research utilizes a flame response model on turbulent jets that includes the necessary details. As a result of this approach, additional equations were added to existing models of turbulent jets that typically describe mean and turbulent quantities. As a consequence, we obtained coupled equations of acoustic-acoercive interactions on the jet flow that can be derived from the energy equation of turbulent jets. Subsequent analysis of these equations, which were simplified along the streamlines of a jet, enabled the assessment of the importance of acoustic-acoercive interactions in various regimes of turbulent jets. As a consequence, we discovered that these interactions can be described by an analytic matrix of interaction coefficients, which can be divided into direct thermal interactions with positive coefficients and indirect interactions with negative coefficients. This matrix can be applied to various flame response models in order to determine their effects on acoustic instabilities in different regimes of turbulent jets. As a consequence of this analysis, it was found that flame response models in turbulent jets generally enhance certain frequency bands in acoustic instabilities. We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on the impact when this interaction breaches the lepton number, which directly leads to a significant influence on the $0\nu \beta \beta$ decay, even when neutrino masses are very small. Since the ultralight dark matter can be adequately modeled as a classical field, this interaction's effect is reflected in a periodic oscillation in the number of decay events. Nevertheless, we find that in the early universe, this interaction would almost certainly disrupt standard cosmological outcomes. Moreover, the condition that neutrinos had to have begun freely moving by the point of matter-radiation equality significantly limits the permissible parameter space, meaning even future $0 \nu \beta \beta$ decay experiments with a meV-scale sensitivity would have difficulty detecting a signal.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical approach to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on associations across the entire genome, by identifying patterns of influence in trait-associated SNPs. This approach can incorporate multiple annotation types and has been successfully applied to eighteen human traits such as blood, platelet counts, metabolism-related disorders, height, obesity, and a bowel disease, as well as two non-coding RNA associated properties. Our results show that most associations fall within previously identified regulatory regions, with two exceptions in transcription factor target sites. We found distinct enrichment of associations in regions with varying levels of accessibility, indicating that different SNPs with accessible or less accessible sites influence traits in different ways, and suggesting that our approach can help in discovering new, unexplored regulatory regions affecting specific traits. By comparing with external data, we suggest that these categories may have different functions and impact transcription at different rates or in various ways.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not
all pertinent research can be covered within this report. It primarily examines
measurements focusing on collective behavior in small systems and new results on
strangeness enhancement observed in proton-proton interactions. It is essential to
note that many notable findings have been excluded from the discussion presented
here.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest a significant population of stellar mass black holes in the region. A crucial aspect of the theory that these sources are actually black holes is the claim that neutron star binaries with low masses exhibit recurring X-ray bursts within short intervals. This study contradicts that idea by revealing that about half of the known LMXBs, featuring a neutron star as the primary component, exhibit outburst recurrence times exceeding a decade when detected by the MAXI telescope. Moreover, to reconcile the total population of neutron star binaries with observed and radio pulsar populations within the Milky Way, researchers find that a significant majority of these binaries have recurrence times exceeding a century for outbursts visible to the MAXI telescope and most remain undiscovered.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized electron spins via vibrational stimulation using THz radiation. By estimating the resulting shifts in energy, new methods for manipulating electron spins via vibrational stimulation and for enhancing the sensitivity of spin sensors through the addition of heavier atomic nuclei are explored.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse, engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces two significant innovations. Firstly, a novel evaluation metric is essential as existing metrics fall short in capturing the concept of response diversity and intent generation. The proposed metric, called Diversity-Sensitive-NLI (DSNLI), leverages Natural Language Inference to assess the variety of responses by examining the validity of statements derived from the conversation's context and responses. The paper's goal is to develop a system that excels at capturing response variety and intent generation, using an annotated dataset consisting of 2,000 examples from the Snips dataset to validate the proposed metric's efficacy. The study reveals that the proposed metric's effectiveness is assured, but the system's ability to generate varied responses is somewhat limited due to the current lack of training data. To overcome this limitation, researchers suggest using a dataset with more varied intents for re-training. Secondly, a new approach is presented to enhance the intent generation capability of a conversation system. By analyzing the conversation's context and estimating the validity of potential responses based on multiple evaluation metrics, a candidate-selection based intent generation strategy is designed. The proposed solution's performance is compared against a baseline, showing a marked improvement in the system's ability to convey varied intents during the conversation.

The occurrence of sustainable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars might be impacted by rotation due to the addition of centrifugal force and potential break-up caused by rapid spinning. Computer simulations model rotating low-mass stars with the capability for sustained nuclear reactions, considering a range of rotation rates, rather than slow rotation alone. Using these simulations, we determined the boundaries within which stars could maintain nuclear energy through hydrogen burning in both radial and axial ranges. As opposed to previous studies that modeled two-dimensional discs, these comprehensive three-dimensional simulations provided more accurate results. For low-mass stars ranging from 0.06 to 0.18 solar masses, we found that faster rotation extending the hydrogen-burning limits of non-rotating objects was not always beneficial, as extreme rotation rates near the point of disintegration led to failed nuclear ignition in some cases.

The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is quite effective, 
However, this analysis faces a major challenge in addressing instrumental influences 
such as fluctuations in background levels and selection efficiency across different 
multidimensional kinematic scenarios.  This article will review traditional methods 
used for calculating efficiency and background probability and discuss the application 
of two techniques specifically density estimation using Gaussian processes and 
artificial neural networks. Although widely adopted in other contexts, these methods 
have not been heavily employed for amplitude analyses. The article also introduces 
new applications for these models, such as leveraging sidebands to determine the 
density of background in multiple dimensions, as well as more comprehensive density 
estimation utilizing artificial neural networks.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the dynamics of afterglows in multiple contexts. Initially interpreted as a pair plasma, the model demonstrates that a magnetic field is generated, enabling it to explain the transition from an electrically neutral state to one capable of producing radio signals. A modified approach to quadrature has been developed to facilitate the estimation of optical flux over time. By applying this model to data from various fireballs recorded by the B612 and B612 CPS systems, intriguing correlations have been discovered when plotting the optical magnitude against the break time in afterglows' light curves. The model's applicability extends to analyzing the properties of dense, opaque plasma and the conditions under which they can exist in a stable state.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of reducing edge crossings within these visualizations can be computationally intensive, yet might not always guarantee sufficiently low crossings levels to maintain the visualization's clarity. In contrast, an approach has been developed to remove edge crossings by splitting specific nodes, targeting the minimum number required to yield an edge-free (planar) drawing. The question of determining if an given bipartite graph can be transformed into an edge-free drawing after minimally splitting nodes from a particular set belongs to the category of difficult problems, whereas establishing a lower boundbelonged to a more manageable subclass of difficult problems. However, this study reclassified it from that subclass to another more intractable one. Additionally, a computationally feasible algorithm has been created to determine the smallest set of nodes to split in order to achieve an edge-free (planar) drawing, given that the given bipartite graph contains a specific substructure belonging to a particular tree-based family.

This paper will present our approach to optimizing bipedal robot walking assisted by thrusters using a closed-loop feedback system. By assuming that supervisory controllers are properly set up to address varying tasks, we will concentrate on refining gait patterns to ensure smooth progression. To address this issue, we will implement a modularity-based strategy comprising two key components: the first is a thruster force regulator that responds to walking discrepancies caused by differences between actual and desired center of mass trajectories; the second involves adjusting step lengths in response to identified differences. The modularity of our proposed framework allows for straightforward integration into existing supervisory controllers and enhances the robustness of robots by reducing reliance on precise mechanical assumptions. The validity and robustness of this method will be demonstrated numerically and experimentally using a Honda HRp-4 robot assisted by thrusters.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific complex-valued field of power series.

In order to enhance side-channel attacks, this research introduces a new technique, HyperDegrade, which incorporates previous methods and employs simultaneous multithreading architectures.  A novel analysis into the causes of performance degradation through cache eviction was also performed, leading to the discovery of an unknown source of slowdowns in 2-way simultaneous multithreading systems.  HyperDegrade was developed without relying on any privileged knowledge, temporal correlations, or required re-execution, and was tested on 12 different applications across multiple PC and Mac machines using full-system emulation.  As a result, HyperDegrade was found to cause an average of 1.5x more performance degradation than other non-invasive side-channel attacks, and up to 2.8x more degradation in certain scenarios.

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be converted into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations, combined with some variations in the diagram configuration, which are referred to as Reidemeister moves. Unknotting operations hold significant value in the field of knot theory; they serve a purpose in analyzing the intricacy of knots and knot-related properties. Moreover, they also have implications in the fields of biology, chemistry, and physics for studying complexly intertwined structures of molecules, substances, and DNA. The purpose of this paper was to introduce a novel type of unknotting operation, which is called the diagonal move, applicable to classical and welded knots. The study shows that the cross-over change, the delta-move, the sharp-move, the gamma-move, the n-gon move, the pass move, and the 4-move can be achieved by applying a sequence of diagonal moves. The study also delves into defining a distance measure that originates from the diagonal move, as well as examining its characteristics.

We've demonstrated that combining the 1-cocycle of a long knot's space with Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles through integration produces a specific Vassiliev invariant, having a precise order of three. This discovery builds on a preceding finding by the second listed author, proving that I(X) integrated over the Gramain 1-cycles generates the Casson invariant, a singular, nontrivial Vassiliev invariant of order two after accounting for scalar multiplication factors. Similarities can be drawn with a part of Mortier's research. Nonetheless, in contrast to but also inspired by his result, we derive our cocycle, I(X), through the use of graph-based configuration space integrals rather than combinatorial approaches used by Mortier.

In cooperative systems with multiple agents, coordination enables tasks to be performed that would be beyond the capabilities of any single agent. We investigate the concept of coordination through strategic decision-making, focusing on a scenario where agents select between two tasks of varying difficulty that are randomly distributed and partially known. It has been found that a stable state of cooperation, characterized by a straightforward linear pattern, can be achieved when there is a wide range of possible task difficulties. Furthermore, it was discovered that the most advantageous action for each agent in response to an approachable strategy profile can be complex and nonlinear when the distribution of task difficulties is not uniform. A computational method has been established to calculate a cooperative equilibrium through learning within the set of linear policy options.

In this context, we explore a privacy-preserving approach called federated learning that enables several entities to train a robust machine learning model jointly, without exchanging sensitive information. Based on how data is held by the involved entities, FL research is divided into two main areas: horizontal and vertical federated learning. Our paper concentrates on addressing challenges in vertical federated learning. Existing methods in this field have frequently relied on idealized assumptions, such as data from different entities having consistent features. Such assumptions, however, are rarely met in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we present a novel VFL method called AlignVFL that can train accurate predictive models using data from multiple entities with varied features, while preserving privacy. AlignVFL combines an alignment technique and a VFL training algorithm to achieve its goal. Notably, AlignVFL needs to resolve multiple optimization issues, deals with noisy labels, and ensures robust multi-party collaboration without compromising security. Our experimental findings show that AlignVFL significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art VFL models in terms of predictive accuracy.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet their scalability to large datasets is severely limited due to the computationally expensive nature of pairwise evaluations. In response, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on larger data sets. While widely adopted, this method has significant drawbacks, notably requiring an unnecessarily large number of features, directly proportional to the size of the dataset, in order to achieve satisfactory results comparable to traditional kernel-based methods. In order to circumvent these limitations and efficiently process large datasets, this paper introduces an alternative method of kernel approximation that leverages insights specific to the underlying data and offers both feature dimensionality reduction and performance enhancements. We test and evaluate this novel method against a range of competitors, including RFF, orthogonal random features, and the Nyström method.

In our study, we demonstrated how both a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner and a diagonal group are effectively incorporated into the wreath products under their combined, or product action, utilizing the Cartesian Decomposition technique.

This research paper examines conformally flat hypersurfaces of n-dimensional space (n is 4 or higher) within a hypersphere of n+2 dimensions. We start by classifying and describing these conformally flat hypersurfaces when they have constant M\"obius curvature under specific transformations. Next, we prove that a compact hypersurface with this constant M\"obius curvature, denoted R, is specifically equal to $(n-1)(n-2)r^2$ for values of r less than 1. Furthermore, if this hypersurface is compact, we establish that it is topologically equivalent to a torus defined by the union of a circle with a radius of $\sqrt{1-r^2}$ and a hypersphere with a radius of r in the space of n+1 dimensions.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created that maximizes energy gain and data transmission efficiency at user terminals. A comparison study with an existing SWIPT method shows the efficacy of the new technique, and various reception techniques at user terminals were examined and compared. Ultimately, an iterative algorithm was developed to solve the information and energy optimization problem, along with power allocation at base station transmitters. A proof of convergence was supplied for the algorithm, and numerical results demonstrated its effectiveness.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers often study network immunization, but traditional methods, such as analyzing the giant component, typically ignore the information gained from removed nodes. This information, however, could provide valuable insights into the spread dynamics. Our study introduces a novel perspective, termed the "avalanche effect," which leverages all node removal data to evaluate the impact of an immunization attack. An avalanche is defined as a batch of nodes that become unconnected to the main component following the removal of a node. We then develop a model, based on a dynamic free energy function, to predict an avalanche's size. This model allows us to retrieve known results, but also offers significant advantages, including an explicit expression for the size distribution of nodes in the main component and the ability to analyze the network's phase transitions under immunization. Our study reveals two distinct phases: one where node removal concentrates within a specific component and another where it spreads to other components. Furthermore, we identify a transitional region in between these phases. Ultimately, our approach utilizes all available information from node deletions, providing a comprehensive analysis of the immunization process.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss in optical recycling systems. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. We present the concept of the sloshing Sagnac interferometer topology, an innovative variation of the Michelson design where the end mirrors are optically linked to form an additional resonating cavity. By transforming the detector into a system with multiple coupled cavities, this design outperforms the conventional signal-recycled Michelson setup by overcoming optical loss-induced limitations. Using advanced parameters similar to LIGO+, this new design offers improved sensitivity at high frequencies or better signal-to-noise ratios for specific binary neutron star merger waveforms, offering promising possibilities for future gravitational wave detectors.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems are considered an exciting development, capable of providing a significant benefit in scenarios with high user density. As a result of scaling the system scale and transmission power while reducing the number of access nodes, extra-extra-large scale MIMO is seen as a promising direction that can further serve to reduce latency and signaling between network elements. In contrast, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces present another option for scaling, offering additional benefits, including enhanced coverage and improved power efficiency by reflecting rather than directly transmitting. In this paper, a theoretical analysis of combined extra-large scale MIMO and RIS, focusing on clustering effects and surface scaling, is presented. In doing so, the surface is treated as more of an architectural design element than a sensing tool. In subsequent analysis, realistic constraints, including surface scaling and transmission bandwidth limitations, are considered. In an initial study of surface scaling and array benefits, real-world measurements were used to validate findings, and they are supported by and extend previous analysis in [1]-[5]. As surface scaling was continued beyond the radio frequency range, a model was developed to predict surface scaling and provide an assessment of how it related to actual measurements. In doing so, an unexpected result of a "scaling barrier" was discovered. In contrast, and building on prior analysis in [6] and [7], a new scaling barrier was presented in [8]. As discussed in [9], three barriers were presented in [10].
